lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Put Harbor Payments before Crestline Logistics in Experience.
items.because: The current order breaks reverse chronology.

items.says: Make the career direction and relevance of the current mechanic role clear.
items.because: The move from operations analysis and an MBA product internship to diesel mechanics may confuse product or operations readers.

items.says: Consider leading with Experience instead of Education for roles that value work history more.
Trim the number of bullets and repeated outcomes, then tailor the remaining details to target roles.
items.because: The résumé has many bullets, including repeated outcomes.

items.says: Shorten the Harbor Payments entry.
items.because: Six bullets are many for a short internship, and several overlap.

items.says: Make the Skills list more targeted and indicate practical depth where useful.
items.because: The list is short and broad, and it does not distinguish familiarity from proficiency.

items.says: Check that the contact details are real, current and clickable.
items.because: The link and contact details look like placeholders.

items.says: Verify that the professional-profile link works and points to the intended profile.
Add a current location if it is relevant to the target roles.
Clarify what “under 5 days per job” measures and, if supported, compare it with prior turnaround time.
items.because: Otherwise, the reader cannot judge the improvement.

items.says: Add the scope or a defensible outcome of the winch and records work.
items.because: The bullet reads mainly as a list of duties.

items.says: Explain how the service records related to the harbor authority’s inspections.
Replace vague wording such as “Owned” and “discussed them.”
items.because: The bullet is less compelling than the quantified bullets.

items.says: Give the scorecards’ scope and the decisions, changes or results they drove, or cut the bullet.
Add the timeframe or error volume, if available.
items.because: That would show the scale of the 30% reduction.

items.says: Specify how forecast error was measured and over what period.
Make the metric label precise for the change from 18% to 11%.
items.because: It is a seven-percentage-point reduction.

items.says: Separate or prioritize the work in the route-planning bullet.
items.because: Combining rollout, SOPs, training and negotiations makes the contribution and saving hard to follow.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 annual driver hours were measured and whether the saving was realized or projected.
Specify whether the four-day onboarding result covers the full pilot or a segment.
Clarify whether the onboarding comparison uses the same cohort or a process baseline.
Describe the 61%-to-66% conversion change in percentage points rather than as a percentage increase.
Clarify whether the checkout result was statistically reliable.
Clarify whether rollout to all merchants was completed during or after the internship.
Explain or verify the support-ticket estimate used for RICE Reach and how the other RICE inputs were handled.
items.because: Tickets prevented can be a proxy, but readers may wonder about Impact, Confidence and Effort.

items.says: Show what the RICE prioritization changed or enabled, if space allows.
Avoid presenting the next-quarter roadmap decision twice.
items.because: This bullet overlaps with the RICE bullet.

items.says: Keep the A/B-test bullet only if it adds a distinct, important detail.
items.because: It repeats the checkout test and conversion result above.

items.says: Clarify the test unit and why session-level randomization was appropriate.
items.because: Repeated sessions from the same users can affect interpretation.

items.says: Keep the presentation bullet only if the funding decision is a separate, meaningful outcome.
items.because: It overlaps with the onboarding result and follow-up roadmap.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the funded rollout.
Clarify whether 3,100 means students reached, eligible users or registered users.
Explain how the nine tonnes of food were measured.
Check that “first year” matches the project dates.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 weekly active users is 187.5%, not 150%.
Specify the weekly-active-user measurement period and, if possible, the timeframe of the growth.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
Clarify how the volunteer system led to the fill-rate improvement.
Say when the fill rates were measured.
Identify the $2.4 million as an estimate or modeled opportunity unless the client realized it.
State your own contribution as team lead.
Clarify what “funded a pilot” means.
Use active phrasing that makes your contribution clear.
items.because: The passive phrasing hides what you did.

items.says: Give the scale or outcome of the intake-form change, or reconsider the bullet if there was no measured outcome.
items.because: It may not add enough beyond the pilot bullets.

items.says: Remove the repeated pilot approval unless the bullet shows a distinct contribution or milestone.
items.because: The savings bullet already mentions pilot approval.
